question.problem: Consider the linear transformation $T:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}4x-2y \\ -10x+5y\end{aligned}]$ and the vector $\,u=[\begin{aligned}k \\ 6\end{aligned}].$ Find the value of $\,k\,$ such that $\,u\in \text{Ker}(T).$

current_example.problem: Consider the linear transformation ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14152450/assets/265758e989d67d0a3deace5bb13bc1831fc9393426301e064fe4161d81a8bddb.svg) and the vector ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14152450/assets/e99158a0f13343581f7dcc66e7ebba503a5923c34d546e14c8217fcc93702780.svg) Find the value of $\,k\,$ such that $\,\mathbf{u}\in\textrm{Ker}(\mathbf{T}).$
current_example.worked_solution:
A vector $\mathbf{u}$ belongs to the kernel of a linear transformation $\mathbf{T}$ if $\mathbf{T}(\mathbf{u})=\mathbf{0}.$ 

So, we need to solve the following equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(u) & =0 \\ [\begin{aligned}3\cdot k+12\cdot 2-3\cdot 6 \\ -2\cdot k+4\cdot 2-2\cdot 6 \\ 6\cdot k-3\cdot 2+3\cdot 6\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}3k+6 \\ -2k-4 \\ 6k+12\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we get the system

$$
\{\begin{aligned}3k+6=0 \\ -2k-4=0 \\ 6k+12=0.\end{aligned}
$$

The solution to all three of these equations is $k=-2.$
